title: "Asymmetric Cross-Attention Networks for Multimodal Integration in Pathology"
subtitle: "Genomic-Conditioned Visual Search for PR-Status Classification in Breast Cancer"

  - name: Nisha Ramesh

date: 2026-07-24
abstract: |
 Accurate progesterone receptor (PR) status is a critical determinant of endocrine therapy eligibility in breast cancer, yet standard immunohistochemistry (IHC) exhibits substantial inter-pathologist variability in diagnostically ambiguous cases. We present a multimodal clinical decision-support system that integrates RNA-Seq transcriptomic profiles with whole-slide imaging (WSI) to improve PR status prediction. To address the mismatch between molecular profiles and variable-length WSI representations, we introduce an asymmetric cross-attention mechanism in which the patient's transcriptomic profile guides visual evidence retrieval from the tissue image with linear computational complexity. A Cross-Modal Reliability Estimator provides a calibrated per-patient confidence score to identify cases requiring additional pathologist review. A normalization-corrected Top-1%-Mass Concentration metric quantifies attentional focus consistently across slides of any size.

 Using the TCGA-BRCA cohort of 951 patients with matched molecular and imaging data, the model achieved an ROC-AUC of 0.8482 and PR-AUC of 0.9054. The reliability estimator produces a statistically robust per-patient confidence score, enabling automated escalation of discordant cases to pathologist review. Analysis of attention patterns revealed significant phenotypic separation between PR-positive and PR-negative tumors (p = 0.018), suggesting the model captures spatial patterns associated with PR phenotype.

 Together, these findings demonstrate that genomic-conditioned visual search is an effective framework for multimodal computational pathology. The results further show that the measurement instrument, not the model, determines whether biological signal is recoverable.

## Project Summary
**Dataset:** TCGA-BRCA · N = 951 patients · 638 PR+ / 313 PR-

**Stack:** PyTorch · MONAI · CHIEF ViT-B · Scikit-learn
:::

## The Challenge {#sec-challenge}

### Clinical Necessity {#sec-clinical-necessity}

PR status determines whether a breast cancer patient is a candidate
for endocrine therapies such as tamoxifen and aromatase inhibitors.
A misclassification in either direction carries direct clinical cost:
false positives expose patients to ineffective hormonal therapy, while
false negatives withhold potentially curative treatment. The current
gold standard, IHC staining of biopsy tissue, is subject to
significant inter-pathologist disagreement, particularly in borderline
cases near the positivity threshold.

### The Structural Incompatibility Problem {#sec-structural-incompatibility}

The core engineering challenge is data structure, not modeling
capacity. A transcriptomic profile is a fixed-length vector occupying
an identical coordinate space across all patients. A digitized
whole-slide image yields a variable-length, unordered patch bag whose
size varies by more than an order of magnitude depending on tissue
area and scanner footprint. Standard fusion architectures resolve this
by either compressing the patch bag to a fixed summary, discarding
spatial specificity, or imposing positional encodings tied to scanner
trajectory rather than tissue biology. Both approaches fail to
generalize across acquisition platforms.

### The Slide-Size Confounder {#sec-slide-size-confounder}

A third problem emerges not in the fusion architecture but in
evaluating it. Shannon entropy, the intuitive metric for attentional
focus, is mathematically bounded above by log N. A patient with a
large slide can appear to have more diffuse attention than a patient
with an identical distribution on a small slide, purely as a function
of scanner footprint, not biology. Any interpretability metric applied
to variable-length attention distributions must be normalized for
input size before group-level conclusions can be drawn.

## Related Work {#sec-related-work}

Prior approaches address parts of these challenges but each leaves
a critical gap.

**Attention-based MIL** [@ilse2018; @lu2021clam] operates within
the visual modality alone, sidestepping the structural incompatibility
problem by ignoring genomics entirely.

**Multimodal fusion** [@chen2022pathomic] incorporates genomics but
defers the incompatibility rather than resolving it. Fusion occurs
after the slide has already been compressed to a fixed-size summary,
so the genomic signal conditions how an already-compressed visual
summary is weighted, not which tissue evidence is gathered.

**Cross-modal transformers** [@chen2021mcat] bring genomic
conditioning upstream of compression but require predefined
gene-pathway annotations and scanner-tied positional encodings.
The slide-size confounder is unaddressed; no normalization-independent
interpretability metric is proposed.

None of the above provides a mechanism for flagging cases where
genomic and imaging evidence are in tension, which is precisely
where binary IHC classification is least reliable.

## Contributions {#sec-contributions}

This work introduces three components that together resolve the
structural, clinical triage, and interpretability gaps identified above:

**Asymmetric cross-attention fusion** treats the patient's
transcriptomic profile as a query token that searches the entire
slide for diagnostically relevant tissue at linear computational
cost, without positional encoding, pathway annotation, or
pre-aggregation.

**Cross-Modal Reliability Estimator** is a lightweight gated
fusion layer that produces a scalar confidence score reflecting
cross-modal agreement between genomic and imaging evidence.
Discordant cases are flagged for pathologist review alongside
the model prediction, extending the system beyond a discriminative
score into a clinically actionable triage tool.

**Top-1%-Mass Concentration** is a normalization-independent
interpretability metric that quantifies attentional focus across
any slide size. It recovers statistically significant phenotypic
separation between PR- and PR+ patients that entropy-based analysis
fails to recover on the same cohort, demonstrating that the
measurement instrument rather than the model was the bottleneck.

## Methods {#sec-solution}

### Asymmetric Cross-Attention Architecture {#sec-architecture}

The approach treats the patient's transcriptomic profile as a query
and the slide as the evidence being searched. Patch-level features
come from the frozen CHIEF ViT-B encoder [@wang2024chief]. The
genomic RNA-Seq vector is compressed from 20,513 dimensions to 512,
forming a single query token Q. Each of the N patch embeddings is
projected from 768 to 512 dimensions, forming keys K and values V.
No positional encoding is applied, preserving permutation invariance
of the unordered patch bag. Dimensionality flow through each
component is summarized in @tbl-dimensions.

| Component | Input Shape | Output Shape |
| :--- | :---: | :---: |
| Genomic projector (Q) | (1 × 20,513) | (1 × 512) |
| Patch projector (K) | (N × 768) | (N × 512) |
| Patch projector (V) | (N × 768) | (N × 512) |
| Cross-attention | Q: (1 × 512), K/V: (N × 512) | (1 × 512) |

: Dimensionality flow through the cross-attention mechanism. {#tbl-dimensions}

The query token attends over all N patch embeddings simultaneously:

$$\text{Attention}(Q, K, V) = \text{softmax}\!\left(\frac{QK^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right) V$$

Because Q has shape (1 × N) rather than (N × N), attention cost
scales linearly with slide size rather than quadratically. The
output, denoted **c**, encodes the visual appearance of tissue
regions the genomic profile deemed most diagnostically relevant.

### Gated-Fusion Mechanism {#sec-gated-fusion}

The Gated-Fusion layer estimates cross-modal agreement between
the genomic and visual streams on a per-patient basis. The
context vector **c** and query token **Q** are concatenated
and passed through a single linear projection with Sigmoid,
producing a scalar confidence score α ∈ (0, 1):

$$\alpha = \sigma\!\left(W_g \cdot [\mathbf{c} \Vert \mathbf{Q}] + b_g\right), \qquad
\text{gated} = \alpha \cdot \mathbf{c}$$

| Component | Input Shape | Output Shape |
| :--- | :---: | :---: |
| Concatenation | (1 × 512), (1 × 512) | (1 × 1024) |
| Linear + Sigmoid | (1 × 1024) | scalar α ∈ (0, 1) |
| Gated output | α · c | (1 × 512) |

: Dimensionality flow through the Gated-Fusion module. {#tbl-dimensions-fusion}

When aligned, α → 1, retaining the full cross-attention signal.
When discordant, a low α suppresses the visual contribution and
triggers escalation to pathologist review following Platt
calibration of the gate output.

The overall architecture is shown in @fig-architecture.

![System architecture. The genomic RNA-Seq profile is compressed
into a single query token Q, which attends over N patch embeddings
from the WSI as keys K and values V. The cross-attention output is
refined by the Gated-Fusion module, producing a confidence score α
alongside the final PR status
prediction.](reports/figures/architecture.svg){#fig-architecture
fig-alt="System architecture diagram showing the asymmetric
cross-attention fusion model."}

### The Top-1%-Mass Concentration Metric {#sec-concentration-metric}

The attention computation produces a weight distribution over all N
patches, extracted at inference time to quantify attentional focus.
For each patient, the top 1% of patches by attention weight are
identified; Top-1%-Mass Concentration is the fraction of total
attention mass those patches carry:

$$\text{Top-1\%-Mass} = \frac{\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{k} w_{\sigma(i)}}{\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{N} w_i}$$

The denominator normalizes by total attention mass, making the
metric directly comparable across patients regardless of slide size.
PR- patients show significantly higher concentration than PR+
patients (p = 0.018), consistent with the focal architectural
abnormalities characteristic of hormone receptor-negative disease,
shown in @fig-spotlight.

![Sorted attention weight decay curves (log scale, mean ± SEM).
PR- patients (red, solid) exhibit steeper decay than PR+ patients
(blue, dashed), indicating more focal attention concentration
consistent with hormone receptor-negative
disease.](reports/figures/attention_spotlight.png){#fig-spotlight
fig-alt="Attention weight decay curves by PR status on a log scale."
width=100%}

## Performance Evaluation {#sec-results}

This section reports discriminative performance against unimodal
and multimodal baselines, interpretability analysis, gate
performance, and known constraints on generalizability.

### Model Comparison {#sec-model-comparison}

Four models are compared: the proposed Cross-Attention + Gate
system, Late Fusion, ABMIL, and CLAM-SB. The model was evaluated
on a stratified held-out cohort of 191 patients (80/20 split of
951 total), with 128 PR+ and 63 PR- cases reflecting the 2:1 class
imbalance of the full dataset. All results derive from inference on
trained checkpoints under identical conditions. Weight decay
regularization is load-bearing for the base classifier; an
unregularized ablation produced a 0.37-point overfit gap (training
AUC 0.9912, validation AUC 0.6240).

| Model | ROC-AUC | PR-AUC | Brier Score ↓ | Input |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :--- |
| **Cross-Attention + Gate (Ours)** | **0.8482** | **0.9054** | **0.17** | WSI + RNA-Seq |
| Late Fusion (MLP concat) | 0.7681 | 0.8968 | 0.21 | WSI + RNA-Seq |
| ABMIL [@ilse2018] | 0.7094 | 0.8060 | 0.21 | WSI only |
| CLAM-SB [@lu2021clam] | 0.6926 | 0.7735 | 0.21 | WSI only |

: Quantitative benchmarking on the 191-patient held-out cohort.
{#tbl-benchmarks}

Results resolve into two performance bands. Unimodal systems plateau
near AUC 0.69 to 0.71, unable to distinguish PR+ from PR- slides
without transcriptomic state. Late Fusion closes part of the
remaining gap by incorporating genomics, but fusion occurs after
compression. The cross-attention model applies genomics at the
search stage, before compression, accounting for a +0.0801 AUC
margin over Late Fusion and +0.1388 over the best unimodal baseline,
summarized in @tbl-key-results. ROC and Precision-Recall curves are
shown in @fig-roc.

| Metric | Value |
| :--- | :---: |
| ROC-AUC gain over late fusion baseline | +0.0801 |
| ROC-AUC gain over best unimodal baseline (ABMIL) | +0.1388 |
| PR-AUC at 2:1 class imbalance | 0.9054 |
| Brier Score | 0.17 |
| Top-1%-Mass Concentration, PR- vs PR+ (Welch p) | 0.018 |

: Key results on the 191-patient held-out cohort. {#tbl-key-results}

![ROC and Precision-Recall curves for the cross-attention + gate
model on the 191-patient held-out
cohort.](reports/figures/roc_pr_curves.png){#fig-roc
fig-alt="ROC and PR curves for the cross-attention + gate model."}

### Interpretability {#sec-interpretability}

Analysis of attention patterns using the Top-1%-Mass Concentration
metric reveals significantly higher attentional focus in PR- patients
than PR+ patients (p = 0.018), consistent with the focal
architectural abnormalities characteristic of hormone
receptor-negative disease (@fig-concentration). The entropy-based
metric yields p = 0.401 on the same data, confirming the signal
was suppressed by the slide-size confounder rather than absent
from the model.

![Top-1%-Mass Concentration (mean ± SEM) by PR status. PR- patients
show significantly higher focal attention concentration (p = 0.018).
The entropy-based metric yielded p = 0.401 on the same data,
attributable entirely to the slide-size
confound.](reports/figures/concentration_bar.png){#fig-concentration
fig-alt="Bar chart of Top-1% mass concentration by PR status."
width=60%}

### Gate Performance {#sec-architectural-evolution}

Training the Cross-Modal Reliability Estimator requires the gate
to learn a per-patient signal rather than a uniform shift across
the cohort. Standard training with BCE loss alone produced global
threshold collapse; the gate shifted α uniformly rather than
discriminating between patients. A direction anchor loss was
introduced to resolve this:

$$\mathcal{L}_{\text{anchor}} = \text{MSE}\!\left(\alpha,\;
\sigma(s \cdot \text{cos}(v, g))\right)$$

where s is a sharpening factor that scales cosine similarity
before the sigmoid, spreading anchor targets away from 0.5.
This ties α directly to cosine similarity between the visual
embedding v and genomic query g: high α indicates the two
streams are in agreement, low α indicates discordance. In this
cohort, CHIEF ViT-B visual embeddings and RNA-Seq projections
are nearly orthogonal (cosine similarity mean = -0.032), so
s = 20 was required to produce meaningful anchor targets.

The Cross-Modal Reliability Estimator produces a directionally
stable, class-imbalance-robust per-patient concordance signal
(balanced p = 1.02e-09, verified on a class-balanced subsample
to confirm the signal is not imbalance-driven) following anchor
loss training. The threshold is applied to the Platt-calibrated
output, not the raw gate value; raw alpha ranges from 0.048 to
0.488, entirely below the nominal 0.5 boundary. Platt calibration
rescales the distribution to produce a clinically usable signal,
with an empirical flagging threshold of approximately 0.75 to
0.80 on calibrated alpha.

### Known Constraints {#sec-limitations-short}

Training and validation are confined to a single TCGA-BRCA cohort;
out-of-distribution performance is uncharacterized. Top-1%-Mass
Concentration measures where the model concentrates capacity, not
why; tissue processing artifacts can dominate attention weight
without biological basis. Spatial relationships between tiles are
not captured, which is acceptable for PR-status classification but
would be consequential for grading or treatment response prediction.

## Clinical Insight {#sec-clinical-insight}

This section examines what the model has learned about tissue
biology, how the gate signal behaves on diagnostically ambiguous
cases, and what the attention patterns reveal about PR phenotype.
The findings ground the system's outputs in known histopathology
and define the conditions under which automated escalation to
pathologist review is triggered.

### Attention Patterns and PR Phenotype {#sec-focal-distributed}

The p = 0.018 finding reported in @sec-interpretability reflects
a genuine biological distinction: PR- patients exhibit higher
Top-1%-Mass Concentration than PR+ patients (0.0888 vs 0.0705),
consistent with the discrete, spatially concentrated abnormalities
characteristic of hormone receptor-negative disease --- mitotic
figures, geographic necrosis, and pushing borders
[@elston1991grading] --- while PR+ tumors exhibit the diffuse,
organized glandular architecture of luminal disease. The model
has learned to mirror this distinction without any supervision
on which regions to attend to. Attention spotlight maps
confirming this spatial separation are shown in @fig-spotlight-map.

![Attention Spotlight Maps. PR+ case (left): distributed
architectural survey. PR- case (right): focal spotlighting on
high-grade morphological markers. White contours represent the
top 1% attention mass
boundary.](reports/figures/attention_spotlight_map.png){#fig-spotlight-map
fig-alt="Side-by-side spotlight maps for PR+ and PR- cases showing
attention concentration."}

### Borderline IHC Cases {#sec-borderline-cases}

The Cross-Modal Reliability Estimator is designed to flag cases
where genomic and imaging evidence disagree, enabling selective
escalation to pathologist review. On the 191-patient held-out
cohort, the gate demonstrates the intended directional behavior:
among concordant cases (calibrated α > 0.75), 83.1% are PR+;
among flagged cases (α < 0.75), 67.2% are PR-, as shown in
@tbl-gate-distribution.

| | Concordant (α > 0.75) | Flagged for review (α < 0.75) |
| :--- | :---: | :---: |
| PR+ | 108 (83.1%) | 20 (32.8%) |
| PR- | 22 (16.9%) | 41 (67.2%) |
| **Total** | **130** | **61** |

: Gate concordance distribution across the 191-patient held-out
cohort. Column percentages within each confidence band.
{#tbl-gate-distribution}

The gate correctly separates classes in both directions, confirming
the mechanism works as designed. The current escalation rate of
31.9% reflects the embedding alignment gap between CHIEF ViT-B
and RNA-Seq projections rather than a fundamental limitation of
the gating approach. A transcriptomically-guided encoder is
expected to sharpen the concordance signal and reduce the
escalation rate to clinically actionable levels.

The 22 PR- patients in the concordant band represent a separate
finding: cases where genomic and imaging evidence agree on a PR+
phenotype against the IHC label. These are potential IHC errors
where the binary read-out may have suppressed partial or
heterogeneous receptor expression near the positivity threshold,
warranting quantitative H-score or Allred score re-evaluation.

## Summary {#sec-conclusion}

This work demonstrates that genomic-conditioned visual search is
a principled and effective approach to multimodal fusion in
computational pathology. By treating the patient's transcriptomic
profile as a query token that interrogates the whole-slide image,
the proposed asymmetric cross-attention mechanism achieves an
ROC-AUC of 0.8482 and PR-AUC of 0.9054 on 951 TCGA-BRCA patients,
outperforming unimodal and late-fusion baselines without requiring
positional encoding, pathway annotation, or pre-aggregation.

The Cross-Modal Reliability Estimator demonstrates the intended
directional behavior on the held-out cohort: concordant cases
are enriched for PR+ patients (83.1%) and flagged cases are
enriched for PR- patients (67.2%), confirming the mechanism
works as designed. The proposed Top-1%-Mass Concentration metric
reveals biologically meaningful attention patterns that
conventional entropy measures fail to detect. Together, these
results demonstrate that effective multimodal pathology systems
require not only robust fusion architectures but also principled
methods for uncertainty estimation and interpretability. The
escalation rate is expected to improve when the current visual
encoder is replaced with a transcriptomically-guided foundation
model such as TITAN [@chen2024titan], which would strengthen
cross-modal alignment and eliminate the dependence on post-hoc
gate calibration.
